name: Level Retest
code:
# Buy when price comes back to a level it has turned at before.
#
# A "level" is a swing point (a bar whose high/low stands above/below its neighbours),
# and levels within `tol` of each other are treated as the same level. `touches` counts
# how many times price turned there, so min_touches=2 means "only levels the market has
# respected more than once".
#
# A pivot needs `right` later bars to confirm it, so a level becomes visible a few bars
# after it forms. That delay is real -- at the moment of the turn nobody knows it was one.

def on_bar(bar, ctx):
    tol = ctx.param('tol', 0.004)
    stop = ctx.param('stop', 0.03)
    take = ctx.param('take', 0.06)

    # ---- manage an open position first
    if ctx.is_long:
        entry = ctx.avg_price
        if bar['l'] <= entry * (1 - stop):
            ctx.close('stop %.1f%%' % (stop * 100))
        elif bar['h'] >= entry * (1 + take):
            ctx.close('target %.1f%%' % (take * 100))
        return

    # ---- look for a retest of established support
    lv = ctx.retest(tol, ctx.param('left', 2), ctx.param('right', 2),
                    ctx.param('lookback', 250), ctx.param('min_touches', 2))
    if lv is None:
        return

    ctx.plot('level', lv['price'])

    if lv['kind'] == 'low':
        ctx.log('retest support %.2f (%d touches, last %d bars ago)'
                % (lv['price'], lv['touches'], lv['bars_ago']))
        ctx.buy(reason='retest support %.2f' % lv['price'])
